summary: Connector queue backlog causing elevated 5xx across API gateway and upstream runtime crashes
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses at the API gateway tied to upstream runtime crash loops. Impact: A subset of dedicated customers (notably Acme Analytics) experienced failures on generate/embed endpoints and intermittent streaming disconnects. Environment: Production (us-east primary, eu-west replica).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a burst of 400 concurrent embedding requests with moderate payloads to /v1/embeddings for tenant=acme-analytics
2) Observe apigw connection queue length and proxy handoff latency rise above baseline (> 500ms)
3) Upstream runtime processes begin reporting GPU driver resets and OOM-like stack traces, returning 5xx to apigw
logs: 2026-03-12T09:42:14Z runtime: gpu_driver: NVML reset observed pid=23754 model=gptj-6b
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Connector (third-party webhook/ingestion) caused burst of retries that backpressured the apigw -> runtime handoff path.
Metric triangulation: apigw accept_queue growth correlated with per-tenant prefetch queue (prefetch_queue_size) increase and increasing NVML reset counts on serving nodes.
We reproduced locally by replaying customer traffic pattern with synthetic retry loops and saw identical accept_queue buildup and subsequent runtime worker restarts.
Observed that a recent routing change (PR #3456) increased parallel prefetch fanout for embedding uploads for dedicated tenants — amplified effect on noisy tenants.
No config change on customer's side. Customer traffic pattern amplified due to external ingestion retries (3rd-party connector).
mitigation_actions: 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC: Emergency rate-limit put on tenant acme-analytics from control plane (soft cap 100 concurrent).
2026-03-12 10:12 UTC: Scaled ephemeral runtime pool by +30% in us-east to buy headroom.
2026-03-12 10:25 UTC: Rolled back routing change from PR #3456 for dedicated embedding fanout (hotfix).
2026-03-12 10:40 UTC: Enabled temporary connector backoff rule on platform ingress to reject obvious retry storms (429 on >5 retries/min).
Result: 5xx rate dropped to baseline within ~30 minutes and runtime crash loops stopped.
comments: Support - Aisha Khan (2026-03-12T09:50): Customer reports mass failures on generate and embed endpoints; opening incident. Notified SRE.
SRE - Tomás Rivera (2026-03-12T10:10): Investigating accept queue and NVML resets. Suspect prefetch fanout interactions. Linking PR and metrics.
SRE - Elena Park (2026-03-12T10:22): Temporarily rate-limited tenant; telemetry shows accept_queue falling.
Customer - Acme (2026-03-12T11:00): Acknowledged reduced errors after rate-limit; provided ingestion connector logs showing repeated 504s from their upstream causing retries.
Support - Aisha Khan (2026-03-12T11:45): Confirmed service recovered; documenting follow-up actions and scheduling postmortem.
resolution: Hotfix: rolled back prefetch/fanout routing change and applied tenant-level soft rate-limit. Added a short-term ingress connector backoff rule to prevent retry storms. Follow-ups scheduled: (1) permanent circuit-breaker for prefetch fanout; (2) tuning NVML driver restart thresholds; (3) add tenant-level early dynamic throttling to prevent accept_queue saturation.
postmortem_followup_items: Create dedicated runbook for connector-retry storms and add to incident playbooks
Automate detection of accept_queue growth and trigger preemptive tenant throttling
Re-evaluate PR #3456 to implement safer gradual rollout and add canary for dedicated tenants
Coordinate with Acme to harden their connector retry/backoff logic
